claims.text: In Edo State, demanding a 'premium' or 'caution fee' beyond rent for a tenancy is unlawful, according to s.6(4) of the Rent Control and Recovery of Residential Premises Edict 1977.
If a landlord demands such a payment, you can recover it or deduct it from your next rent.

For monthly or quarterly tenancies in Edo, a new tenant who has paid rent in advance has a statutory six-month breathing space before a landlord can give notice to quit, as stated in s.18 proviso of the same Edict.

post.headline: Edo State: Pay the rent, not the premium

If you're a new tenant who paid rent in advance for a monthly or quarterly tenancy,
you get a six-month breathing space before a quit notice (s.18 proviso).

short.title: Read your tenancy agreement. Or pay twice.
short.hook_say: Before you sign that tenancy agreement, read it. Many tenants sign without understanding the clauses, only to find themselves paying for things they didn't agree to. Don't pay twice for the same thing.

tips.say: In Edo State, the law (s.6(4) of the Rent Control Edict 1977) makes it unlawful to demand any premium or caution fee beyond the actual rent. Know this to avoid paying extra.
If an illegal premium is demanded and paid in Edo, you have the right to recover that payment. You can even deduct it from your next rent payment without penalty.

For new tenants in Edo, if you've paid your rent in advance for a monthly or quarterly tenancy, the law gives you a six-month statutory breathing space before a landlord can issue a quit notice (s.18 proviso).
Always get a proper tenancy agreement. It outlines your rights and obligations, ensuring your tenure is protected and preventing future disputes. DocOga helps you make one fast.
